title: Phase 1 QA
eyebrow: QA · roadmap phase 1, approvals and the design loop just work, issue #493, plugin 2.78.0

short.lead: Phase 1 is built on the branch AjsAgent/session-handoff as plugin 2.78.0: seven steps, issues #501 to #507. Everything that can run outside your own desktop app has now run. verify.py passes 1135 of 1135 checks and tools/verify_tools.py 52 of 52. 14 real headless Claude sessions (sessions with no screen) took a test repo through the whole design loop using only this branch's plugin, and all 14 did what the design says. Real branch switches and a real merge passed 6 of 6 checks. The hooks run as fast as those in 2.76.0, and 2.78.0 installs straight from the branch, so you can try it without merging to main.
short.hint: Tap a row to see what was run and what it showed.
items: "Demo widget design approved 1A" moves the stage
A live headless session (claude -p, plugin loaded from this branch) in a throwaway repo got "Demo widget design approved 1A". The stage file then said Plan, feature "Demo widget". Step 1, #501.
The next live session got "don't Design approved: Gadget". The stage stayed Plan with the feature "Demo widget". Step 1, #501.
An approval after a cloud system note counts

A live session got a message that opened with a system-reminder block, the way cloud sessions deliver your words, then "Design approved: Gadget 2B". The stage moved to Plan with the feature "Gadget". Before this phase, the whole message was read as a relayed notice and moved nothing. Step 1, #501.
A build plan approval reads the issues from GitHub

Run against this repo, the new read returned exactly #493 and #501 to #507, all labelled, in 0.7 seconds. The helper's first version used gh issue list, which cloud sessions refuse with a 403 error, so it was switched to GitHub's REST API issue list (a plain web request that cloud sessions allow). Step 3, #503.
Design to Build to QA, in real sessions

Live sessions 1 to 4: "Widget design approved 1A" moved to Plan, "Issues for Widget: #10 #11 #12" recorded the issues, "Widget build plan approved" moved to Build, and a real Edit of app.py went through. The script and its saved output are in docs/plans/2026-11-11-phase-1-live-tests/.

Live sessions 13 and 14: a reply that ended with the line "Design approved: Gadget" was recorded as the one line offered, and the next message, just "Approve 2B", moved the stage to Plan with the feature "Gadget". The old feature "Widget" was kept with its issues. verify.py also covers a reply offering two lines (moves nothing, says why). Step 2, #502.
One message sends a fault back to Build

Live sessions 5 to 9: once the issues said needs review, the stage moved to QA and an edit was refused. "QA failed: Widget the button is grey" moved it back to Build with all 3 issues kept. An edit was still refused while the issues said needs review, and went through once they were back to in progress, with no bounce back to QA. Step 4, #504.
Four ways around the code lock are closed

Real git, real hooks: after checking out an older branch, the code edit was refused with "Write Continue from: older"; a new approval there released it. After a real merge of a branch in QA into main, an edit on main got the Done-stage message, not the QA lock, and the stage file was left unchanged. Two more cases are in verify.py: a stage file hidden in .git (case D3), and a new name keeping the old feature (case D6, also seen live in session 14). Step 5, #505.
Design points come back to you

Live sessions 10 to 12: a reply ending "Should the button be blue or green?" set the hold; the next message, "Blue" plus an edit request, cleared it and the edit went through. A reply of "I went with option B for the layout." was sent back once and rewritten. The rule text has no "unless they have said otherwise" exception (verify.py). Step 6, #506.
The close line is offered; the label line is said once

verify.py cases: when a QA-passed feature's pull request merges, the note offers you "Close as completed: ..." with its issues. The end-of-reply label reminder is said once per set of wrong labels instead of on every reply. 15 proof cases cover the eight audit findings already fixed and old issues #102, #107, #110, #128, #129 and #130. Step 7, #507.
No slower; installs from the branch

Timed five times each on a fresh clone: the end-of-reply hook takes 0.79 s (2.76.0: 0.82 s), the others 0.05 to 0.06 s, every exit code 0. In an empty Claude config, adding the marketplace as https://github.com/Ajw2003/AjsClaudeCodeTools.git#AjsAgent/session-handoff and installing gave 2.78.0; adding the plain URL back and reinstalling gave 2.76.0.

unverified: Your desktop app on Windows: every run was on Linux, in this cloud container. The new code reads files and runs gh (the GitHub command-line tool) the same way the existing hooks do, but it has not been run on Windows itself
The real Approve button in the claude.ai app: the live sessions sent the text "Approve 2B", and whether the app's button sends exactly its label has not been seen
Real GitHub labels and issues in the live loop: those sessions used the plugin's stand-in files; the GitHub read itself was run once against this repo and returned #493 and #501 to #507
The close-line offer after a real pull request merge: only replayed merge events have run (verify.py)

wrapup.summary: QA for phase 1: every test that can run here passed; what is left is the four items listed as unverified.
wrapup.changing: Plugin 2.78.0 on the branch AjsAgent/session-handoff, which also carries the session handoff work. Nothing reaches main until you merge a pull request.
wrapup.blocking: Your QA verdict. If you want to try it first, 2.78.0 can be installed from the branch and removed again without touching main.
wrapup.next: If QA passes, I open a pull request to main that says Refs #493, and offer you the close line for #501 to #507 after it merges.
